title: print check comes first
body: Before cutting any fabric, measure the calibration square on page 1 of your printed pattern. If it isn't exactly 3 cm, fix your printer scale — everything depends on it.

title: invisible zippers go in early
body: For an invisible zipper, install the zipper first and only then close the seam below it. Doing it the usual way round is the most common reason they turn out wavy.
source: University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension FCS2-842

title: learn on real garments
body: The courses that keep beginners sewing all do the same thing: a small set of core skills practiced on 2-3 complete garments, not isolated drills. Finish things — that's the skill.

title: stretch seams need backup
body: Putting a zipper into a stretchy fabric? Stabilize the seam allowance with lightweight nonwoven interfacing first so the seam doesn't ripple.
source: University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension FCS2-842

title: firm for tailored, soft for flowing
body: Tailored designs need firm fabrics. Soft fabrics belong in flowing designs with ease or gathers. Match the fabric's drape to the silhouette before you fall in love with a print.
source: University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension CT-MMB.180

title: beginner-friendly fabric picks
body: Starting out? Medium-weight, firmly woven fabrics are the kindest — cotton and cotton blends are a good choice. Slippery satins and loose weaves fight back; save them for later.
source: University of Kentucky Cooperative Extension CT-MMB.180
